=== F1 (BLOCKING): _is_stale_only_rejection's substring match is defeated by author-controlled text, and silently disarms BOTH protections the second review round was added to preserve ===

scripts/lwb_lanes.py:808
    return len(record_errors) == 1 and "STALE" in record_errors[0]

The docstring above it argues this is safe because "STALE" is "its only use anywhere in this module outside prose comments -- see the STALE branch of _review_ok". That is true of where the marker is WRITTEN and false as a guarantee about what the string CONTAINS. Every one of _review_ok's failure messages interpolates values the record's own author controls:
  - {rel}, the record's path -- and reviews/README.md says in terms: "The filename does not matter."
  - {data.get('verdict')!r}
  - {shared_segment!r}, in the self-review collision message.
So a rejection for a reason that is NOT staleness can carry the literal marker "STALE", satisfy len(record_errors) == 1, and be reclassified as routine churn: moved out of `errors`, demoted to a NOTICE, and the gate passes.

REPRODUCTION, run against this branch's own scripts/lwb_lanes.py using this branch's own test helpers (tests/test_lwb_lanes.py::_write_review_pr), PR 56 so the >= REVIEWER_ID_FORMAT_CUTOFF_PR identity rules apply. Each case is one DISAGREE-or-collision record plus one fresh valid AGREE (REQUIRED_INDEPENDENT_REVIEWS = 1, so the AGREE is sufficient on its own).

  (a) CONTROL -- self-review identity collision, shared token 'plaintok1':
        independent_reviews(...) -> ok = False            [correct: gate fails]

  (b) SAME collision, shared token renamed to 'STALEtok1':
        independent_reviews(...) -> ok = True
        errors  = []
        notices = ["not counted toward the 1 valid review(s) above, but enough already exist: reviews/56/collide.json: reviewer_id and commit_author_id share the segment 'STALEtok1' (9 characters, at or above MIN_SHARED_SEGMENT_LENGTH=8) -- likely the same session or dispatch reviewing its own work, not an independent reviewer"]
      A detected self-review passes the gate. The only difference from (a) is five characters in a self-attested identity string.

  (c) A live DISAGREE in a file named 'reviewer-B-NOT-STALE.json':
        independent_reviews(...) -> ok = True
        errors  = []
      The gate passes with an unaddressed DISAGREE sitting in the directory.

  (d) Same as (c) at PR 9 (below the identity cutoff), for completeness:
        errors  = []
        notices = ["not counted toward the 1 valid review(s) above, but enough already exist: reviews/9/disagree-but-NOT-STALE-reviewer.json: verdict is 'DISAGREE', want 'AGREE'"]
      The notice text is worth reading twice: a live objection, reported in words as a wrong verdict, filed under "enough already exist".

WHY THIS IS BLOCKING RATHER THAN A ROBUSTNESS NOTE. c04be73's entire reason for existing is the narrowing: the first version of this fix downgraded every rejection reason, a prior independent review caught it, and the narrowing was the remedy. This PR's body states the property as preserved -- "a DISAGREE verdict or a self-review identity collision sitting in the same directory still does [veto]". Measured at this head, both are defeated by a rename. The repository already has the motive in its own history: PR #46's title is "drop two unclearable stale DISAGREE records", i.e. removing a reviewer's dissent is an operation this repo performs. After this change, the same effect is available as a one-word rename of someone else's record that leaves the record in place and produces a green gate and an approving notice.

It is also not a future hazard. The reviewer of PR #55 flagged the substring coupling as a robustness note, conditioned on "IF a future rejection message ever contains the word STALE for another reason". I am not re-filing that note: the interpolation of {rel} means every existing message already can, today, at this head, with no code change -- which is what (b) and (c) demonstrate and what moves it from robustness to a live bypass.

SUGGESTED FIX (small, and it does not require touching _review_ok's signature, which the docstring names as the binding constraint). Have the STALE branch append to a caller-visible sentinel rather than a free-text marker -- e.g. _review_ok appends a module-level STALE_PREFIX constant at the START of its message and _is_stale_only_rejection uses record_errors[0].startswith(STALE_PREFIX) with the prefix placed before {rel}; or have the STALE branch set a one-element flag list passed in alongside `errors`. Either removes author-controlled text from the decision. A regression test should assert case (b) and case (c) above fail the gate -- I could not find an existing test that would have caught either, and I looked (see WHAT I DID NOT CHECK).

=== F2 (NOT BLOCKING): the new hook is inert for git cherry-pick, which is the operation this repo's recovery workflow actually uses ===

scripts/githooks/commit-msg's header states it "moves the check to the moment the commit is written". git does not run commit-msg for cherry-pick, rebase, am, or format-patch application, and cherry-pick PRESERVES the original author. Measured in a throwaway repo (not committed anywhere), hook installed via core.hooksPath:
    poisoned commit authored 'LEAPWare-HQ <leapware@outlook.com>' on a side branch
    git cherry-pick <poisoned>   -> ACCEPTED, hook never ran, resulting author still 'LEAPWare-HQ <leapware@outlook.com>'
    git rebase main              -> ACCEPTED, hook never ran (author here happened to be clean)
    git merge --no-ff <poisoned> -> merge commit itself is clean, but the poisoned commit becomes reachable and the hook cannot see it
This is the exact defect class the hook exists to preempt, on the exact operation ("re-cut from the last good commit") the last five re-cuts used. NOT blocking, and I want to be precise about why: scripts/lwb_check_commit_identity.py still runs in CI over the full base..head range and does catch every one of these, so the hook is incomplete defense-in-depth, not a vacuous check. I verified that too -- see the mutation probes below, and note that the CI script scans `git log base..head`, which includes cherry-picked and merged-in commits. What I am charging is the header's unqualified claim, and the missed opportunity: one sentence naming cherry-pick/rebase as uncovered would stop the next session trusting the hook through a re-cut.

=== OBSERVATIONS, RAISED NOT CHARGED ===

- _review_ok evaluates the VERDICT check before the STALE check, so a DISAGREE that is also stale is reported as a wrong verdict, never as STALE, and therefore vetoes forever. This is unchanged behaviour (before this PR every rejection vetoed), so it is not a regression and I am not charging it -- but it means a dissent over content that no longer exists is unclearable except by deleting the reviewer's record, which is what PR #46 did and what reviews/README.md elsewhere calls falsifying evidence. Worth an explicit decision rather than being discovered again.
- The hook has NO automated test in this repository: `grep -rln "githooks" tests/` and `grep -rln "commit-msg" tests/` both return nothing. The body's evidence is a manual transcript in a throwaway repo, uncommitted. I reproduced every claim myself (item 5) so I am not calling it unproven -- but a shell hook mirroring a Python allowlist BY HAND, with the sync obligation written only in a comment, and no test asserting the two agree, is the drift the header itself warns about with nothing mechanical behind the warning.
- The hand-mirrored allowlist already differs in a small way: the Python BOT_NAME/BOT_EMAIL use \w (Unicode-aware in Python 3 str patterns), the shell uses [[:alnum:]_.-] (locale-dependent). No realistic bot name distinguishes them; recorded for the sync obligation, not charged.
- THE HOOK IS OPT-IN, AND I AM MYSELF A LIVE EXAMPLE OF WHAT THAT COSTS. In this container `git config core.hooksPath` was UNSET, so scripts/githooks/commit-msg would not have run at all; and my own configured identity when I arrived at this branch was `Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>` -- bit for bit the #54 poison. Had I committed this review record as I found things, I would have produced the sixth unrecoverable bad-identity commit in one day, on the very PR whose purpose is to stop them, and the hook shipped here would have been silent. I set `git config user.name/user.email` and `core.hooksPath=scripts/githooks` repo-locally before committing, and the hook then accepted my commit. Not charged against this PR -- the header says plainly "Not installed by cloning" and names the enable command -- but it is the measured reason F2 matters: a hook that every session must remember to enable protects exactly the sessions that were already going to get it right. Something that installs or verifies it (a documented setup step every session runs, or a CI check that the hook file and lwb_check_commit_identity.py's allowlist still agree) would close more of this than the hook does alone.
- --no-verify bypasses the hook entirely. Inherent to every git hook and backstopped by CI; named only so nobody reads the hook as a guarantee.

=== NEAR-MISSES OF MY OWN, PRINTED AS REQUIRED ===

TWO, both caught before they became false accusations.

FIRST. I ran the self-review-collision variant of F1 at PR 9 and got ok=True with errors AND notices both EMPTY. I was about to report something considerably worse than F1 -- a collision accepted with no error and no notice at all, the repository's own "could not check is indistinguishable from checked and found nothing" defect shape. It was my error: _write_review defaults to pr=9, which is below REVIEWER_ID_FORMAT_CUTOFF_PR (19), so the identity-collision check is CORRECTLY skipped for that record and nothing was being silently swallowed. I re-ran at PR 56 with an explicit control case (a) and only then did the real finding stand up. Had I filed the PR-9 result I would have charged this PR with a defect that does not exist, and the control is the only reason F1 is stated at the severity it actually deserves.

SECOND. I mutated HANDOFF.md's proof count from 23/23 to 30/30, ran `python scripts/lwb_handoff.py --check`, got "passes all checks" and rc=0, and had "the handoff check is vacuous for the count it exists to record" half written. Wrong target: lwb_handoff.py --check is a STRUCTURAL check, and the count is guarded by lwb_check_state_claims.py, which caught the falsified value immediately and precisely ("recorded=['30/30 proven'] re-derived=['23/23 proven']"). Both run in CI (.github/workflows/ci.yml:180,184). I had measured a real behaviour of the wrong script and was about to attribute it to the repository as a hole.

Separately, on PR SELECTION rather than on this PR, and repeating a defect the #55 reviewer also reported: my instructions say to skip a PR whose reviews/<pr>/ holds a record naming the CURRENT HEAD SHA. Read literally that is unsatisfiable -- committing a review record advances the raw head, so no committed record can ever name it, and all 13 open PRs would need re-review on every run forever. The gate does not work that way: resolve_reviewable_head skips record-only commits. I computed the REVIEWABLE head for all 13 open PRs by importing lwb_lanes and calling it, and 12 of 13 already carried a record naming the code they contain (#40, #44, #45, #46, #47, #48, #49, #51, #52, #53, #54, #55). Only #56 was genuinely unreviewed. The cost of the literal reading is visible in this repository right now: reviews/40/ holds SEVEN records and reviews/44/ holds FIVE, nearly all naming a single reviewable head. This is a defect in the reviewer routine's own instructions, not in any pull request.
